svg.text: TWO ARGUMENTS, AND THEY ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS
Pixelate — any diagram can be REDRAWN rectilinearly
Thread — rectilinear diagrams can be BUILT for every n
The first converts what already exists; the second produces them from scratch. Both are checked below.
any Venn diagram
A
B
C
three circles: 8 regions
the same diagram, pixelated
A
B
C
staircase curves: still 8 regions
PIXELATION: REPLACE EACH CURVE BY THE OUTLINE OF THE SQUARES IT COVERS
Square k belongs to set i when its centre does. The new boundaries are staircases, so rectilinear.
Every region contains a disc; once the mesh is smaller than that disc, the region keeps a square,
so no region is lost. For the three circles, mesh 0.5 down to 0.1 all worked — except one:
at mesh 0.15 two squares of one region met only at a corner, splitting it. A tiny shift of the grid repaired it.
pinch
SO “FINE ENOUGH” IS NOT QUITE ENOUGH — IT MUST ALSO BE GENERIC
A corner touch is fatal twice over: the region falls apart, and the outline is no longer a simple curve.
Only finitely many grid placements produce one, so almost every offset avoids it. Sampling 12 random
offsets: 10 of 12 worked at mesh 0.4, 11 of 12 at mesh 0.15, and 12 of 12 at mesh 0.1 — the bad
placements thin out as the mesh shrinks.
THREADING: THE CONSTRUCTION OF PROBLEM 2, RUN AGAIN
A curve crossing every face once doubles the region count. Applied to the 5-set diagram: its 32 faces
form a graph of degrees 3, 4 and 5, a Hamiltonian cycle was found, and threading it gave a 6-set diagram.
64 regions, all present, all connected — verified at spacing 1/28
Corners used: 4, 4, 4, 4 for the rectangles, then 24 for the fifth curve and 52 for the sixth.
